text:
kai: Heads up — RFC followup: proposal to migrate admission/control from lease-token broker to a 'credit shepherd' service. Reason: smoother cross-proxy smoothing and simpler edge backpressure.

maria: tl;dr — one-time migration plan? :eyes:

kai: yeah. plan sketch: 1) introduce shepherd as read-only observer consuming admission events; 2) parity mode where shepherd suggests deltas; 3) edge / admission subscribe to shepherd decisions via a light shim; 4) cutover with canary by namespace.

anna: what's the latency budget on decisions? we can't add >5ms to p95.

kai: shepherd will be eventual + cached. Real-time decisions remain local for strict SLOs; shepherd provides smoothing hints and rebalancing signals. Local admission still authoritative.

sam: so shepherd = coordinator for redistributed credits, not authoritative token source? Sounds safer.

kai: exact. authoritative stays local. shepherd issues 'soft-credit' recommendations and long-window allocs.

lee: any proto/config? quick sketch:

```
message CreditHint {
  string namespace = 1;
  int64 suggested_pool = 2; // tokens/sec
  int64 window_ms = 3; // smoothing window
  enum Mode { OBSERVE=0; RECOMMEND=1; ENFORCE=2; }
  Mode mode = 4;
}
```

maria: love that. How do we avoid oscillation when shepherd recommends drops back to edge?

kai: use hysteresis + momentum. shepherd exposes confidence and trend. edge applies low-pass filter.

devops: telemetry wise we need new metrics: shepherd_recommendation_delta, edge_applied_fraction, recommendation_confidence. Add tracing tag for decision_id.

ops-bot: deploy-hook: shepherd service v0.1 deployed to staging :sparkles:

sam: migration timeline? canary namespaces and a safety kill-switch if applied_fraction spikes < 0.2.

anna: and rollback steps? revert edge shim and let local admission run. we should also include a feature-flag gated path.

kai: agreed. I'll draft a brief runbook: canary 10 namespaces, 1h steady state checks (latency, error, token drops), then 25%, 50%, 100% over 48h. Will post RFC update with runbook and feature flags.

maria: assign owners? kai + devops for shepherd, anna + lee for edge shim, sam for telemetry.

lee: I'll add the shims to the admission repo and open PR with toggles.

sam: quick note — update alert thresholds for smoothed backpressure so SRE doesn't flood on expected shepherd-induced drops.

kai: good call. I'll add alert updates to the runbook.

maria: :thumbsup:

kai: thanks all — I'll follow up with the RFC patch and runbook by EOD.
